content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use family nouns and possessive adjectives my, your, his, and her. Model: “This is my sister. Her name is Anh.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use people in my family clearly and politely. One useful response is: “This is my sister. Her name is Anh.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where people in my family is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about people in my family.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Use family nouns and possessive adjectives my, your, his, and her.
objectives: Use family nouns and possessive adjectives my, your, his, and her.
Use family words in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about people in my family.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about people in my family. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: Who is Mai?
listening.transcript: This is my uncle. His daughter is my cousin, Mai.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Keep his and her short; stress COU-sin. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Keep his and her short; stress COU-sin.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about people in my family.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using people in my family; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise people in my family?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: This is my sister. Her name is Anh.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about people in my family with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about people in my family. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: This is my sister. Her name is Anh. Submit your draft first.
